reviewer: error_driver; independent of adapter/tests/CLI author; own GUI excluded
scope: Full installed held-lease range adapter header/source, full reader test and full thin CLI, with core planner/accumulator and existing day reader/profile/file-IO source context.
assessment: The adapter borrows exactly one valid held lease and uses its directory descriptor. Fixed stats/YYYY/MM/DD.dat names are generated only from the admitted plan. It acquires no additional lease, reads no clock/cache/config/payload-derived path and performs no write.

Selected directories are inspected without following symlinks, require owned physical directory type, open with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, and compare initial named/opened/current identities. Relevant symlinks, regular-file directory substitutes and FIFOs are rejected before content access.

Selected day files require owned regular type, open O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, compare named versus opened dev/inode/uid/mode/nlink/size/mtime/ctime, enforce 1MiB before allocating, and retain that exact descriptor through strict parse and final fd/path identity checks. Ancestor names and the held root are checked before publication; replacements/truncation observed by these checks fail.

All inventory has fixed three-level recursion and constant descriptor depth; every non-dot entry, including inert/cache/non-date names, consumes the 65536-entry count. Only exact valid years/months/DD.dat dates are followed. Relevant date paths must be physical owned directories/regular leaves; scan errors, stop, changed identities/timestamps, future-only first date or excessive final plan fail. The core independently bounds actual selected dates/buckets before data accumulation.

One <=1MiB string and one bounded record vector are read/parsed at a time. Records move into append, never accumulate all input files. Early file/parser/arithmetic/limit/allocation failure returns unexpected; the partially filled local accumulator is destroyed. finish is called only after every planned date and final root/cancellation checks.

Stop is checked around directory/file reads, each content-read iteration, parser, append, inventory iteration and final publication. A stop observed alongside injected EIO has cancellation precedence. Missing, present empty/header-only and observed zero remain distinct.

The 16 source test families have substantive independent signed six-field, inclusive-whole/exclusive-bucket, filename-spill, coverage and ownership assertions. Read wrappers call __real_read first and arm only matching generated dev/inode. Replacement/truncation/month-swap cases assert both fired and mutationOk; middle-file cancellation asserts the second selected file was read. readdir mutation/cancel/IO wrappers match the real directory descriptor; the flood seam feeds inert names to the actual production entry counter, with exact cap and cap+1 outcomes.

Tests create only explicitly owned /tmp/biglybtc-history-range-tests-* fixtures, hold leases before preservation stamps, compare bytes/dev/inode/mode/nlink/size/mtime/ctime and avoid atime claims. Unsafe-target sentinels remain unchanged; parsed output outlives the lease. CMake enables only target-private read/readdir wrappers on this test; the CLI has no such substitutions.

The CLI parses exact explicit period/offset/now arguments, obtains one requested lease, invokes the actual range API once and prints returned primitives/optionals. It mirrors no accounting arithmetic, invokes no Java, has no implicit profile or now, and prints unknown six-tuples as dashes. Output begins only after a complete successful API result.
review_limits: Source-only review: no compiler, native/Qt/Java execution, profile access, operational-script import/evaluation, Git command or network. Actual 16-family results belong to root qualification; no author-reported execution adopted as reviewer execution.
Individual file/path checks and All inventory are not a transactional multi-file snapshot and cannot exclude every unobserved same-user race. This is explicitly stated by the API and source capsule.

The inventory flood uses a synthetic readdir provider; it proves the production count gate, not a physical directory containing 65537 distinct files. Memory failure is source-mapped to Io, not exhaustively allocation-fault injected here.

The comparison CLI expects its caller to choose generated profiles; it has no generated-path authorization fence. ProfileLease::acquire can create/use the ordinary .azlock, so adapter data-read-only scope does not mean the entire CLI performs zero filesystem writes.
No new Java equality or whole Statistics/global accounting/runtime parity credit is claimed.
